Saudi Arabia's decision to join the US in strikes against targets in Iraq marks a new phase in the regional war.
Riyadh had been reluctant to retaliate despite repeated attacks on its territory and US military assets based there.
But after a Saudi Aramco refinery in Jazan was hit, Saudi Arabia joined Washington in strikes on more than 20 targets across seven Iraqi provinces.
The attacks targeted Iran-backed groups as well as Iranian advisers, sending a warning to Iraqi militias and Yemen's Houthis against further attacks.
The strategy appears aimed at keeping the response limited while Saudi Arabia continues back-channel diplomacy with Qatar and Pakistan to contain the conflict.
But Riyadh risks being drawn into a wider war as the US seeks greater regional backing for its campaign.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States is no stranger to extreme weather — but it's getting worse. Wildfires now burn through more than 3 million hectares a year, almost double the rate of the 1990s. Floods, both major and minor, are hitting somewhere in the country on 8 out of every 10 days. Storms and hurricanes are intensifying too, with more Category 3+ storms on record than ever before.
But disasters aren't the only threat. Summers themselves are getting hotter and longer — and the extreme heat driving that shift is quietly becoming one of the biggest risks to public health and the environment alike.
From wildfires to floods to rising heat, Americans are learning to adapt to a new climate reality.

Hundreds of people have been forced to flee their homes, with some returning to devastating scenes of destruction.

Scientists warn climate change is making wildfires more intense and creating conditions that make them harder to contain.
With another heatwave forecast, officials fear the worst of Europe's wildfire season may still lie ahead.

description:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says US President Donald Trump has agreed to give Ukraine licences for the domestic production of Patriot missiles. Washington has not confirmed the deal.
Ukraine has long sought Patriot systems to strengthen its air defences against Russian drone and ballistic missile attacks.
Zelenskyy later visited the US Congress, where senators overwhelmingly voted to advance a sweeping bill of tougher sanctions against Russia. 

Ukrainian authorities say Russia has attacked a civilian cargo vessel off the Black Sea port of Odesa.
Moscow says the ship was carrying military equipment. 
Smoke was seen rising from the Liberian-flagged ship after the strike.
Officials say the vessel had been unloaded, and no crew members were on board at the time.
They say it's the third Russian attack on a civilian ship in the area.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.
